CEO Letter: Unlocking Enterprise Use Cases with Gen2X
summary: Impinj Gen2X speeds inventory, increases tag read range, declutters environments, protects consumers, inhibits label and item counterfeiting and reduces cost.
body_text: CEO Letter: Unlocking Enterprise Use Cases with Gen2X Impinj Gen2X speeds inventory, increases tag read range, declutters environments, protects consumers, inhibits label and item counterfeiting and reduces cost. For nearly two decades, Impinj has stood at the forefront of RAIN RFID , helping visionary Fortune 500 enterprises solve tough operational challenges. For example, self-checkout and loss prevention at a visionary European retailer, loading and shipping accuracy at a major global logistics provider and food inventory at a leading grocery chain. Solving these challenges led us to develop key RAIN innovations – a solutions toolbox – that we call Impinj Gen2X . Today, we are releasing Impinj Gen2X to the RAIN industry. Gen2X is an enhancement to the radio and logical layers of the RAIN (Gen2) industry communications standard that speeds inventory, increases tag read range, declutters the environment, protects consumers, inhibits label and item counterfeiting and reduces solution cost. As one of the contributors to Impinj Gen2X, I am personally thrilled by its release. Always part of the plan Back in 2004, as the Gen2 working group developed the RAIN standard, we knew we couldn’t anticipate the needs of every enterprise in every industry. So, we created a standard that incorporated those things we did know, while leaving the door open for solution providers to innovate on top of the standard. If the innovations proved broadly useful then future versions of the standard could add them. If features were narrowly useful or out-of-scope then they would remain the domain of individual solution providers. Over the years Impinj developed many such innovations. Some made it into Gen2V2, standardized in 2014 and Gen2V3, in ISO standardization now. Some remained narrowly useful or out-of-scope. And some were works-in-progress that missed the standards-development timeline. Gen2X is a toolbox with our key innovations, some standardized and some not, that we use to solve enterprise challenges. Our goal in releasing Gen2X broadly to the industry is to accelerate RAIN adoption. Seamless interoperation, available to all In our experience, enterprises want to know (1) does Gen2X interoperate seamlessly with the RAIN standard and (2) is it available to all solution providers? The answer to the first question is yes. The answer to the second is we have already given Gen2X royalty-free to all leading reader manufacturers, including Zebra Technologies, and our Gen2X patents are included in our cross license with our primary endpoint IC competitor. Looking forward, if parts of Gen2X prove broadly useful then we will consider contributing them to the next version of the RAIN standard. “As RAIN RFID becomes increasingly essential to leading global enterprises, Zebra and Impinj are driving innovations that deliver the item visibility those enterprises need,” said Joe White, chief product and solutions officer at Zebra Technologies. “Zebra, as a Gen2X licensee, plans to leverage Gen2X in our products and solutions. We look forward to the benefits Gen2X will have enhancing item visibility and creating operational success for our customers.” Unlocking enterprise solutions today and tomorrow At the most fundamental level, Gen2X either solves previously unsolvable use cases, reduces solution cost or both. For example, Gen2X reduces retail-inventory counting time, saving labor cost. It declutters conveyor-to-truck shipment loading, reducing costly misshipments. Its decluttering also improves retail loss prevention, allowing consumer self-checkout. It boosts dock-door directional accuracy, reducing costly shipping mistakes. It improves the readability of small, embedded tags or tags on hard-to-read items, reducing tag cost and enabling new use cases like food tagging. It addresses consumer privacy at point-of-sale. And Gen2X is not static – we continue adding new innovations to it. We are today focused on enterprise use cases, but tomorrow’s emphasis will be on consumer use cases, including consumer safety and item sustainability. And always on reducing solution cost. I truly believe that RAIN will connect trillions of everyday items. Today, our industry isn’t even at the 1% point. Gen2X can, I believe, accelerate that path to trillions. So I invite every industry participant to use Gen2X , as we together connect every item in our everyday world. And to see Gen2X in action, visit the Impinj booth at NRF 2025 in January. title: Como gerir contratos de longa duração com fornecedores?
summary: Aprenda a gerenciar contratos de longa duração com fornecedores a partir das 7 melhores práticas + quais são os principais desafios e como enfrentá-los.
body_text: Os contratos de longa duração com fornecedores requerem atenção extra dos gestores e time de compras e procurement por serem mais estratégicos, formalizar um nível de comprometimento mais expressivo e abrangente entre as partes envolvidas e exigir um acompanhamento pontual e constante. Se por um lado, gerir acordos de longo prazo é um tanto complexo, por outro, esse tipo de relacionamento comercial é bastante benéfico. Entre os pontos positivos estão questões como estabilidade no fornecimento, alcance de padrões de qualidade mais consistentes e diminuição do risco de desabastecimento. Porém, para obter bons resultados como esses, o segredo está em realizar uma gestão de contratos de longa duração com fornecedores que considerem todos os desafios, prós e contras desse tipo de documento. Neste artigo, trouxemos as sete melhores práticas para você realizar esse gerenciamento e construir relacionamentos mais sólidos com seus parceiros comerciais. Confira! Quais as diferenças entre contratos de curto prazo e duradouros com fornecedores? Formalizar uma parceria comercial por meio da assinatura de um contrato é primordial para assegurar os direitos e deveres do fornecedor , mas também os da sua empresa. O motivo é que esse documento registra todos os pontos acordados e evita desentendimentos futuros, a exemplo de discussões sobre quantidades e periodicidade de abastecimento. Entretanto, existem algumas diferenças significativas entre a gestão de contratos de longa duração com os fornecedores e os de curto prazo. Conhecê-las é essencial para você realizar uma gestão eficaz e livre de erros. Estes são os principais pontos que diferem um do outro: nível de comprometimento : contrato normal : não há a necessidade de construir uma relação comercial de confiança, pois é firmado apenas para atender a uma demanda pontual e não recorrente; contrato duradouro : exige a construção de relacionamentos estratégicos com os fornecedores , visto que inclui critérios como alinhamento de necessidades e expectativas em longo prazo; flexibilidade : contrato normal : dispensável pelo fato de conter condições de contratação específicas para atendimento de uma necessidade pontual; contrato duradouro : requer cláusulas que assegurem ajustes a partir de critérios como mudanças de mercado, econômicas ou tecnológicas; monitoramento constante : contrato normal : desnecessário por ter um ciclo de duração curto; contrato duradouro : essencial e deve incluir KPIs ( indicadores de desempenho ) para mensurar a performance do fornecedor durante a validade do acordo de longo prazo; riscos : contrato normal : baixos e comumente relacionados a falhas pontuais; contrato duradouro : inclui riscos estratégicos e de mais impacto para a empresa contratante por conta do tempo de duração. Leia também: “ O que faz um gestor de contratos? Entenda sua importância! ” Quais são os desafios da gestão de contratos de longa duração com fornecedores? Além de entender as diferenças, para realizar uma boa gestão de contratos de longa duração com fornecedores, você precisa conhecer os desafios envolvidos. Essa é a melhor maneira de se preparar para superá-los e, dessa forma, proteger a sua empresa e extrair o melhor de um relacionamento comercial mais extenso. Esta é a lista com os problemas mais comuns e algumas formas de resolvê-los: adaptação às mudanças : a exemplo de alterações do mercado e necessidades dos clientes finais. Solucione com a inclusão de uma cláusula de revisão periódica do documento e critérios sobre o que e como revisar; criação de dependência : monte um cadastro com fornecedores qualificados e comprovadamente aptos para atender a sua empresa tão logo haja necessidade; fluxo de monitoramento : adote ferramentas de automação que realizem a gestão de contratos automaticamente e emitam alerta de revisões e renovação de documentos; acompanhamento dos padrões de qualidade : resolva por meio da definição e aplicação de KPIs específicos para o gerenciamento de fornecedores, feedback de consumidores finais e auditorias; gestão de relacionamento com os fornecedores: defina políticas internas, qualifique, avalie e monitore as empresas fornecedoras continuamente. Use soluções como um SRM (Supplier Relationship Management) para automatizar e otimizar essas atividades. Dica! Confira como funciona o SRM da Linkana! Como realizar uma renegociação de contratos com fornecedores de sucesso? 4 dicas! Para realizar uma renegociação de contratos com fornecedores de forma eficiente, segura e benéfica para todos os envolvidos, considere cenários internos e externos, aponte prazos para revisões periódicas, insira cláusulas especiais no documento e estimule o aprimoramento contínuo da parceria comercial. Entenda os detalhes: considere cenários internos e externos : pontos como chegada de novas tecnologias, alterações no comportamento do consumidor final e de objetivos do negócio refletem diretamente nas necessidades de abastecimento, tanto de itens quanto de quantidades; aponte prazos para revisões periódicas : a fim de evitar contratos obsoletos, desalinhados com as mudanças, que gerem prejuízos financeiros às partes ou aumentem os riscos; insira cláusulas especiais : a exemplos das voltadas para confidencialidade, penalidades em caso de não conformidade ao longo da parceria comercial e critérios para ajuste de valores; estimule o aprimoramento contínuo : por meio de estratégias como definição de metas de performance, cláusulas bônus por desempenho e reuniões regulares para dividir conhecimentos e alinhar expectativas. 7 melhores práticas para gestão de contratos de longa duração com fornecedores Quer realizar a melhor gestão de contratos de longa duração com fornecedores para a sua empresa? Então, adote estas práticas: estabeleça uma boa comunicação; compartilhe metas, objetivos, expectativas e resultados; defina indicadores claros e justos; mantenha a flexibilidade e a adaptabilidade; determine cláusulas para resolução de conflitos; realize auditorias periodicamente; automatize a gestão de contratos. 1. Estabeleça uma boa comunicação Evitar ruídos na comunicação é essencial em qualquer relacionamento comercial. Porém, quando se trata de uma gestão de contratos com foco em longo prazo, é ainda mais importante, pois você terá contato com o fornecedor por muito tempo. Assim, contradições simples podem se tornar problemas expressivos. Evite esse tipo de problema com estratégias como: estabelecimento de canais oficiais de conversa, troca de informações, envio e recebimento de documentos e pedidos; definição de um responsável para lidar diretamente com o fornecedor; conversas e reuniões regulares. 2. Compartilhe metas, objetivos, expectativas e resultados Dessa forma, os fornecedores saberão exatamente o que sua empresa precisa para crescer e têm a chance de trabalhar para contribuir com esse propósito. A dica aqui é dividir esses dados via relatórios, mas se atentar para compartilhá-los de uma maneira que chame a atenção do fornecedor e os faça entender seus objetivos. Portanto, evite simplesmente enviar os números. Agende uma conversa para explicar os pontos principais e tome cuidado para não compartilhar informações confidenciais. 3. Defina indicadores claros e justos É fundamental monitorar os contratos continuamente para verificar o cumprimento das cláusulas e os resultados dessa parceria de longo prazo. Aqui, o ideal é definir e adotar indicadores de desempenho como: eficiência logística; taxa de conformidade de qualidade; capacidade de resposta; taxa de ocorrência de não conformidade; nível de serviço ( SLA ); percentual de produtos rejeitados/devolvidos. Dessa forma, você trabalha com dados e não com achismos, tem uma visão real da performance dos fornecedores e parâmetros para decidir se segue com a renegociação do contrato de longa duração ou não. 4. Mantenha a flexibilidade e a adaptabilidade Facilite a adoção de uma postura flexível e adaptação na gestão de contratos por meio do acompanhamento das mudanças relacionadas ao seu ramo de atuação, chegada de novas tecnologias, tendências e comportamentos de consumidores. Ao expandir o seu conhecimento, você facilita a comunicação com os fornecedores, constrói diálogos mais benéficos para ambos e rompe barreiras com potencial de atrapalhar a inovação no fluxo de abastecimento do seu negócio. Sugestão de leitura para você: “ O futuro das vendas: como as tecnologias podem redefinir o setor? ” 5. Determine cláusulas para resolução de conflitos As cláusulas para resolução de conflitos buscam evitar disputas entre as partes durante a validade desse documento. O objetivo é garantir os direitos, mas também os deveres de cada um em questões como valores, condições de pagamento, frequência na entrega e nível de qualidade. Defina quais serão essas cláusulas dos seus acordos de longo prazo, principalmente a partir da análise dos riscos gerados pelos fornecedores. Inclusive, temos um artigo sobre esse tema que ajudará você. Veja! “ 5 erros na avaliação de riscos de fornecedores e como evitá-los ” 6. Realize auditorias periodicamente Um bom monitoramento de contratos inclui auditorias constantes. A prática é a melhor maneira de identificar falhas da sua empresa e dos seus parceiros comerciais, como desvio de dinheiro e corrupção de fornecedores , que prejudicam seriamente o seu negócio. Aproveite e leia também: “ Como fazer checklist de auditoria de fornecedores? Para que serve? ” 7. Automatizar a gestão de contratos A tecnologia é sua melhor aliada na gestão de relacionamento com fornecedores, em especial os de longa duração. Por meio de sistemas de gerenciamento de contratos, fica muito mais fácil emitir, conferir, colher assinaturas, organizar, armazenar e monitorar contratos. Se contar com uma solução integrável a outras, sua rotina se tornará ainda mais prática e eficiente. O SRM da Linkana **, por exemplo, se integra a todos os ERPs e também a sistemas como os de compras e de fornecedores. ** Com a nossa solução, você otimiza o tempo de homologação de fornecedores, realiza monitoramentos automáticos e conta com diversas outras funcionalidades, por exemplo, gestão por categoria, recebimento de documentos e formulários diretamente na nossa plataforma. Solicite agora uma demonstração e confira, na prática, tudo o que a Linkana oferece para a sua empresa!

body_text: What is this for? Imagine you were a salesperson from Facebook/Meta using ZI Sales to find potential buyers for your products, and you filter for companies making $750K or above and located in Maryland. The search result returns 163,138 companies — a daunting number. Naturally, you would focus on the top results first to identify potential customers. As a salesperson, you would also want the top results to be the most likely customers, not just some random order. Currently, there is a relevance ranking applied that doesn’t consider the tenant offerings. This project aims to address this by implementing a new relevance ranking system that takes into account the correlation between users’ products and the search results, providing more relevant outcomes. How does it work? The specific relevance ranking that was the subject of this project is powered by what’s known as boosting logic. This process involves boosting on (i.e., emphasizing) certain attributes of a company to determine its score. Companies with higher scores rank higher in the results. To implement this new boosting logic, we examine the tech attributes relationship among our vendors , categories , and products . Vendors refer to companies selling products , which fall under specific categories , further classified into parent and child categories. Tech attributes simply refer to the identification of these vendors, categories, and products. Note: I will refer to the parent category as “top category” and child category as “category” from now on. You can actually see this relationship defined in the technologies filtering in ZI Sales: Here, the vendor is “Facebook, Inc.”, selling “LiveRail” as their product, which falls under the category “Ad Exchanges” and top category “Advertising”. If a user adds this filtering to their search, the resulting companies would be those using LiveRail. This project applies similar logic to the results, but instead of filtering for a specific product, we boost on the category/top category associated with the products the vendor (user) sells. In action, consider the salesperson scenario from before: their 161,138 results would now be ranked by whether the companies use products under the categories of products Facebook sells, such as Advertising/Ad Exchange in the case of LiveRail. In the big picture, this means our vendors will receive tailored results based on their products’ category/top category, rather than seeing the same results ranked by popularity boosting. How do we implement it? First, let us review the information we have. We have a database about tech attributes, including product names, their associated categories/top categories, and vendors. By leveraging this data, we can modify the original boosting logic to prioritize boosting based on tech categories instead. As for the actual implementation, it consists of a two-step process: creating a database and developing a service to query it. Creating the graph Our tech attributes data is initially stored in a relational database. However, to better analyze the relationships between the data, we convert it into a graph database using Neo4j. Graph databases are designed to handle complex relationships more efficiently than relational databases. They consist of nodes (entities), edges (relationships), and properties (attributes), which allow for a more intuitive representation and analysis of interconnected data. After importing the data into Neo4j, we can perform specific queries based on the nodes’ properties and relationships. Neo4j also provides a visual representation of these nodes and relationships, which helps in understanding the data connections. Here’s an example of how this would look like with sample data about movies and actors (taken from [1]). In this example, we submit a query to find the list of movies that the actor, Tom Hanks, has acted in. The resulting graph with the actor node in the center and the movies around the center node is shown below. Creating the service With the graph database set up, the next step is to create a service, which I chose to develop with NestJS/Typescript. The goal of the service is to query a vendor’s category or top category. This involves creating a single endpoint that accepts a parameter identifying the vendor and returns the relevant category or top category. If a vendor has multiple categories, further logic determines which categories to return and prioritize for boosting. Aside from the service logic, additional configurations are necessary during the development process, such as creating a Dockerfile and setting up a Jenkins build for CI/CD. Does it work? The objective of this project is to develop a better boosting logic that returns specific results based on user persona. In theory, boosting on a vendor’s tech categories should provide more relevant potential customers. But does this hold true in practice? To determine this, we need to conduct testing. This involves comparing the top 25 results from our current boosting with those from the new tech attributes boosting. To achieve this, we need to obtain actual user searches, filtering those queries to focus on vendor companies, and then comparing the top 25 results between the two boosting methods. We have found indications illustrating how the new boosting logic does indeed yield relevant outcomes. Example Specifically, let us examine the top 25 results for the company “Hexnode”. Comparing the old and new boosting logic, we found a difference of 19 companies in the top 25 results. This means that 19 different companies appeared on the first page of results with the new boosting logic. Here’s a screenshot of the results, with their rank changes noted, where “company1” is from the original boosting and “company2” from the new boosting. What’s notable is that for the first three new companies that appear, they all have been tagged by the user, suggesting they are considered relevant. This means that even though these companies were not initially on the first page of results, the user still found them and deemed them relevant. With this new boosting logic, we can push these companies to the first page, enhancing their visibility. What’s next? In the further development of this project, several considerations can be made: Currently, the user-specific boosting logic applies only to companies selling products, which represents just a subset of our users. If we could expand it to other users, such as those providing services, more users would get tailored results. Vendors often have multiple categories, making it essential to choose the most relevant ones. The current logic in the service can be improved to achieve this, but it requires more comprehensive data. The graph database can be further utilized and expanded to consider other important relationships, which could enhance the boosting logic or lead to other improvements in ZI Sales. References [1] https://neo4j.com/docs/getting-started/appendix/tutorials/guide-cypher-basics/

With just a few commands, you’ll have a fully operational LLM management backoffice up and running. Ready to deploy with Docker? Check out our detailed Docker deployment guide for step-by-step instructions on setting up phospho with Docker. Quick and Simple Steps to Deploy phospho 1. Prerequisites: 1. Create a Propelauth Account Propelauth handles authentication and security. Sign Up: Create your Propelauth account 2. Obtain an OpenAI API Key You'll need an OpenAI API Key for analytics and clustering features. Get API Key: Register and obtain your OpenAI API Key 3. Register for MongoDB MongoDB serves as your database. Choose between a local installation or MongoDB Atlas cloud service. Sign Up: Register for MongoDB 4. Install Docker Docker containerizes your application to ensure consistency across environments. Install Docker: official Docker installation guide . 5. Set up Google Cloud Platform (GCP) The GCP Natural Language API detects language and sentiment in user messages. Get Started with GCP: Google Cloud Platform 6. Set up Temporal Temporal manages jobs and long-running computations. Get Started with Temporal: Get started guide 2. Clone the Repository The first step is to get the source code. Open your terminal and run: git clone <https://github.com/phospho-app/phospho.git> This clones the phospho repository to your local machine. 3. Create Your Environment File Configuration is streamlined with an .env.docker file. Simply create this file in the root directory of the project and paste the following template: # Application Environment APP_ENV=local ENVIRONMENT="test" # API Configuration API_VERSION=v0 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_VERSION=v0 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 LOCAL_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 NEXT_PUBLIC_LOCAL_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 # Authentication Settings NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_URL=https://<your_id>.propelauthtest.com PROPELAUTH_API_KEY= PROPELAUTH_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback PROPELAUTH_VERIFIER_KEY=-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY----- PROPELAUTH_URL="https://<your_id>.propelauthtest.com" # GCP Configuration GCP_PROJECT_ID="" GCP_SERVICEACCOUNT_EMAIL= GCP_PRIVATE_KEY=-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- GCP_JSON_CREDENTIALS_NATURAL_LANGUAGE_PROCESSING= GCP_JSON_CREDENTIALS_BUCKET= # OPENAI API Key For Chat and Embedding models OPENAI_API_KEY= OPENAI_BASE_URL= # MongoDB Database Configuration MONGODB_NAME="test" MONGODB_URL="" # Local Development Settings TEMPORAL_HOST_URL=host.docker.internal:7233 TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE=default TEMPORAL_MTLS_TLS_CERT_BASE64= TEMPORAL_MTLS_TLS_KEY_BASE64= # (OPTIONNAL) Services and Integrations RESEND_API_KEY= STRIPE_SECRET_KEY= STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET= SENTRY_DSN= EXTRACTOR_SENTRY_DSN= SLACK_URL= AZURE_OPENAI_KEY= AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT= TEST_PROPELAUTH_ORG_ID= TEST_PROPELAUTH_USER_ID= Fill in your credentials, and copy the file into the platform , ai-hub , and backend folders. 4. Run Temporal (Optional for Development) If you need Temporal for workflow management, you can start it locally with: temporal server start-dev --db-filename your_temporal.db --ui-port 7999 This step is optional if you are not working with Temporal-dependent features. 5. Start phospho with Docker Compose Now for the magic. Simply navigate to the project directory and run: docker compose up Docker Compose will handle building and running the entire phospho platform. No need to worry about dependencies or environment mismatches—it just works. Why Choose phospho with Docker? Ease of Setup: Minimal configuration means you’re ready to go in minutes. Consistency Across Environments: Whether you’re on your local machine or deploying to a server, Docker ensures everything works seamlessly. title: Maximize Savings on Commercial EV Chargers
summary: Discover federal, state, and utility incentives to save on commercial EV charger installation. AmpUp helps you unlock big savings.
body_text: First, let’s talk about the federal tax credit. Known as the Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Credit , it’s a program that covers up to 30% of the cost of commercial EV chargers and their installation, capped at $100,000 per charger. Your business’ refueling property must be placed in service in an eligible low-income community census tract or non-urban census tract – and the good news is that around two-thirds of Americans are in eligible census tracts. You can learn more here . This can significantly reduce upfront costs for commercial installations, making it easier for businesses to join the EV revolution. But the savings don’t stop there. While the federal credit is a fantastic baseline, your state and local utility may have even more to offer. State-Level Incentives: Tailored to Your Location Across the US, states support EV adoption through tax credits, grants, and rebates for EV chargers. The National Conference of State Legislatures ( NCSL ) says that “as of July 2021, at least 47 states and the District of Columbia offer incentives to support the deployment of EVs or alternative fuel vehicles and supporting infrastructure, either through state legislation or private utility incentives within the state.” However, the availability of these incentives, terms, and amounts vary depending on where the commercial EV chargers will be installed. For example: Connecticut is launching AmpUp Adapt in 2025 with support from a state grant. It’s a pilot project in partnership with AmpUp for up to $25,000 in funding for Level 2 EV chargers for commercial, multi-family, or public properties in Connecticut within the Eversource service territory. California provides robust funding options through programs like CALeVIP , which are aimed at expanding EV infrastructure throughout the state. A new program will launch in 2025. New York supports businesses through the NYSERDA Charge Ready NY program, which offers up to $4,000 rebates per Level 2 charging port for commercial installations. To explore what’s available in your state, the US Department of Energy offers a searchable database of incentives. It’s an excellent resource for finding state-specific opportunities that fit your business needs. You can check that out here. Utility Rebates: A Hidden Gem In addition to state-level programs, utilities often offer rebates or incentives for installing EV chargers. These programs are designed to encourage businesses to help build a more robust charging network while balancing grid demand. For example, AmpUp is partnered with Eversource in Connecticut to streamline access to the utility’s Level 2 EV charger rebate program. Businesses can receive up to $25,000 per site for installation costs, significantly reducing the financial barrier to entry. Utility programs can sometimes be less well-known, but they’re worth exploring. They often provide generous support that can make a big difference in your bottom line. How AmpUp Can Help You Navigate Incentives With experience working on state-level programs and utility-level rebates, AmpUp has helped businesses nationwide unlock significant savings. Our team works closely with you to identify all the incentives you qualify for, ensuring your EV charging project is as cost-effective as possible. Whether you’re a small business or managing a large commercial property, AmpUp’s expertise and software simplify the installation process from start to finish. Why Now Is the Time to Act Financial support is available to help you install commercial EV chargers. title: High Power Density in Batteries
summary: Higher power density batteries deliver more power in a shorter time, a good fit when quick bursts of energy or high-power output is required.
body_text: What is power density in batteries? Power density in batteries refers to the amount of power a battery can deliver relative to its size or weight. It is typically measured in watts per volume (W/cm³) or watts per unit weight (W/kg). Higher power density batteries can deliver more power in a shorter time, making them a good fit for applications that require quick bursts of energy or high-power output. How does power density affect battery performance? Batteries with higher power density can release energy quickly. This is important for devices or situations requiring rapid power bursts, like electric vehicles accelerating or drones taking off. These batteries also perform well under high-load conditions because they can sustain their voltage and power output, ensuring a stable and reliable power supply in demanding situations. Batteries with a higher power density are more efficient in energy conversion. They can better convert stored energy into useful power, minimizing energy loss as heat during battery discharge. With high-power density, batteries can be smaller and lighter while maintaining performance. This, again, is a key factor for portable devices and electric vehicles where size and weight constraints exist. There is one key consideration when it comes to the performance of these batteries. High Power density is crucial for immediate power needs, but it can affect battery longevity due to increased stress from rapid charging and discharging, which accelerates degradation, potentially reducing its lifespan. However, advancements in battery management systems and cooling technologies are helping mitigate these effects in modern batteries. What are common applications for high-power density batteries? High Power density batteries have diverse uses across various industries. As noted, they are integral to the success of EVs , providing the rapid bursts of power required for acceleration and supporting regenerative braking, which results in extended driving ranges and faster charging times. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles ( UAVs ) rely on high-power density batteries for liftoff, stability, and efficient flight control. High Power density batteries can store and deliver more energy in a compact size, allowing UAVs to fly for longer periods without the need for frequent recharging. This is particularly valuable for drones used in surveillance, inspection, or delivery services. Electric aircraft are another segment in which these batteries could prove indispensable, facilitating short-haul electric air travel by delivering rapid power for propulsion while maintaining energy efficiency. These batteries could also aid in emergency response and disaster relief equipment, enabling the rapid deployment of critical tools and devices during emergencies. Other potential applications that would benefit from reliable, high-power density batteries include medical devices, power tools, and industrial equipment. What are the benefits of high-power density in batteries? Faster Charging Times High Power density batteries can be charged more quickly due to their ability to accept a higher rate of energy input. This is an advantage in various applications, such as electric vehicles, in which reducing downtime is essential. Higher Energy Output These batteries provide a higher rate of energy delivery, ensuring that devices and systems can operate at their peak performance. In electric vehicles, for instance, this translates to improved acceleration. Improved Performance The ability to provide quick bursts of power enhances the overall performance of devices and equipment. For instance, power tools equipped with high-power density batteries can handle demanding tasks quicker and more effectively. Versatility High Power density batteries can be used in various applications, from electric vehicles to aerospace, making them versatile and adaptable to different needs. Reduced Footprint These batteries can achieve high performance in a smaller, lighter package, making them ideal for portable devices and space-constrained applications. What are the challenges of achieving high-power density in batteries? The Cost of Development Developing batteries with high-power density typically involves using advanced materials and manufacturing processes . These materials can be expensive, so creating batteries with these materials may result in higher production costs. Balancing the need for performance improvements with cost-effectiveness can be a challenge. Manufacturers try to find ways to reduce production costs without compromising the performance and safety of high-power density batteries. This includes optimizing production processes and sourcing cost-effective materials. Energy Storage Capacity High Power density batteries are designed to deliver energy rapidly, but this can sometimes come at the expense of energy storage capacity. In batteries, optimizing energy density and power density is often a trade-off. Designing for high power output can limit the battery’s ability to store large amounts of energy due to constraints in cell chemistry, thermal management, and structural design. Achieving this balance is crucial, as a battery with very high-power density but inadequate energy storage may not be practical for many real-world applications. Heat Management The process of rapid energy discharge generates heat, which can accelerate degradation of the cell materials, impacting battery performance and creating potential safety concerns. Efficient heat management ensures the battery stays within a safe temperature range during operations. Inadequate heat dispersal can lead to overheating, which may reduce battery lifespan or cause thermal runaway. Managing heat involves the development of effective cooling systems, thermal insulation, and intelligent battery management systems that can manage power output to prevent overheating. Manufacturers and researchers are constantly working to find solutions that balance high-power density, cost-effectiveness, energy storage capacity, and adequate heat management to create high-performance batteries that can meet the demands of various applications. What battery technology advances impact power density? Silicon Anodes and Nickel Cathodes Silicon anodes can store more lithium ions compared to traditional graphite anodes. This storage capability enables higher energy density and, consequently, increased power density. Silicon anodes are known for their ability to deliver rapid power output, making them one potential path for improving battery performance. Amprius has been active in their research and development in silicon anode technology, which has played a pivotal role in improving their battery performance, particularly regarding rapid power output and higher energy storage capacity. In August 2023 , the company unveiled an ultra high-power, high-energy lithium-ion battery, built on its Silicon Anode Platform. Cathodes have also played a significant role in advancing battery performance. High-nickel-content cathodes offer improved energy density and power density . These cathode materials allow for faster charging and discharging rates, resulting in high-performance batteries. Electrolytes Advanced electrolyte formulations enhance ion conductivity for quicker charge and discharge rates in batteries. This directly impacts power density by allowing for rapid energy delivery. Battery Management and Thermal Systems “Smart” battery management systems with advanced algorithms and real-time monitoring are tasked with optimizing the charging and discharging of the batteries. They ensure safety, reliability and efficiency of the battery system by managing parameters such as voltage, current, and temperature. Efficient thermal management systems, including integrated cooling and heating mechanisms, are another way to help regulate a battery’s temperature. Manufacturing and Production Techniques Innovations in battery manufacturing, such as roll-to-roll production , lead to more cost-effective production of high-power density batteries. This lowers production costs and increases the accessibility of advanced battery technology. Using nanomaterials and nanostructures in battery components enhances ion transport and electron flow. This results in faster charging and discharging rates, ultimately improving power density. Materials and Architectural Innovations Incorporating advanced, energy-dense materials into batteries increases power density while maintaining energy storage capacity. Lithium-sulfur and lithium-air batteries , for example, have the potential to enhance rapid power delivery significantly. Innovations in energy storage architectures maximize the surface area for energy transfer and storage, leading to higher power density. Three-dimensional (3D) electrodes and micro-supercapacitors are examples of these architectural advancements. Important factors to consider when selecting a battery with high-power density Selecting a battery with high-power density requires a thoughtful evaluation of critical factors to match the specific needs of your circumstances: Understanding the power requirements is the first step, considering peak and sustained power demands. Balancing high-power density with adequate energy storage capacity is essential to ensure consistent performance, especially in uses with intermittent high-power needs. Verifying the battery’s voltage and current ratings align with your equipment’s requirements is important for compatibility and safety. Temperature tolerance, cycle life and charging efficiency also deserve careful consideration to guarantee optimal battery performance. The chosen battery chemistry should align with the specific demands of your application, and cost-effectiveness should be weighed against the advantages of high-power density. Physical characteristics, such as weight and size, should match any space constraints. Consider durability, maintenance requirements, and regulatory compliance in your decision-making process. Finally, it is vital to assess the battery’s performance over its lifecycle as well as compatibility with your charging and discharging systems. By balancing these factors, you can select a high-power density battery that aligns with your situational requirements and delivers the expected performance and efficiency.

title: Firefly Awarded $179 Million NASA Contract for Moon Delivery to Gruithuisen Domes
summary: Firefly's third lunar mission will deliver and operate six NASA instruments in the Gruithuisen Domes on the Moon’s near side in 2028.
body_text: Company’s third lunar mission and fourth NASA CLPS task order utilizes Firefly’s Blue Ghost lunar lander, Elytra Dark orbital vehicle, and a rover to operate six NASA instruments Cedar Park, Texas, December 18, 2024 – Firefly Aerospace, Inc. , the leader in end-to-end responsive space services, was awarded an approximately $179.6 million NASA contract to deliver and operate six NASA instruments in the Gruithuisen Domes on the Moon’s near side in 2028. As part of NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload (CLPS) initiative, the mission will utilize Firefly’s Blue Ghost lunar lander, Elytra Dark orbital vehicle, and a rover from an industry provider to investigate the unique composition of the Gruithuisen Domes – a part of the Moon that has never been explored. “Firefly is proud to land our fourth NASA CLPS award for another complex mission, which is what our team does best,” said Jason Kim, CEO of Firefly Aerospace. “This incredible team gained a hard-earned reputation for smooth payload integrations, well-rehearsed operations, and robust testing and transparency throughout Blue Ghost Mission 1 preparations. As Firefly works towards becoming the go-to commercial company to provide autonomous systems on the Moon and beyond, our robust line of vehicles stand ready to deliver a historic mission to the Gruithuisen Domes.” During mission operations, Firefly’s Elytra Dark transfer vehicle will first deploy the Blue Ghost lander into lunar orbit and then remain on orbit to provide long-haul communications. Blue Ghost will then land in the Gruithuisen Domes, deploy the rover, and support payload operations for more than 14 days on the lunar surface. The NASA payloads onboard Blue Ghost include the Radio-wave Observations at the Lunar Surface of the photoElectron Sheath (ROLSES) telescope, the Sample Acquisition, Morphology Filtering, and Probing of Lunar Regolith (SAMPLR) robotic arm, the Neutron Measurements at the Lunar Surface (NMLS) instrument, the Photovoltaic Investigation on the Lunar Surface (PILS) instrument, and the Heimdall camera system. The mission will also carry NASA’s Lunar Vulkan Imaging and Spectroscopy Explorer (Lunar-VISE) payload with multiple instruments attached to both the lander and rover to determine the composition of the Gruithuisen Gamma Dome. Considered a geologic mystery, the Gruithuisen Domes appear to be composed of silica-rich volcanic minerals, which could indicate the presence of lunar water and hydrogen. The NASA payloads onboard Blue Ghost Mission 3 will investigate the formation and physical properties of the domes, including the potential detection of water and hydrogen molecules, in addition to other science investigations. “Firefly is dedicated to flying annual missions to the Moon for both government and commercial customers as we continue to pave the way for a lasting lunar presence,” said Brett Alexander, Chief Revenue Officer at Firefly Aerospace. “We’re seeing growing interest from organizations looking to unlock the Moon’s resources and build a robust lunar ecosystem, and we welcome additional partners to join us.” Along with the NASA payloads, Firefly’s mission has capacity for additional customers, offering orbital transfer and long-haul communications in cislunar space on Elytra as well as lunar surface delivery and operations on Blue Ghost. Customers interested in joining Blue Ghost Mission 3 can find more information at https://fireflyspace.com/missions/blue-ghost-mission-3/ . Firefly’s first mission to the Moon, Ghost Riders in the Sky , is on track for launch in mid-January 2025 with 10 NASA payloads onboard Blue Ghost. Firefly’s second lunar mission is scheduled to launch in 2026, utilizing a similar two-stage spacecraft configuration as Blue Ghost Mission 3, with the Blue Ghost lander stacked on Elytra Dark to support payload operations on the far side of the Moon and in lunar orbit. About Firefly Aerospace Firefly Aerospace is an end-to-end responsive space company with launch, lunar, and on-orbit services. Headquartered in central Texas, Firefly is a portfolio company of AE Industrial Partners (“AEI”) focused on delivering rapid, reliable, and affordable space access for government and commercial customers. Firefly’s small- to medium-lift launch vehicles, lunar landers, and orbital vehicles provide the space industry with a single source for missions from low Earth orbit to the surface of the Moon and beyond. title: Introducing S2
summary: Introducing S2, a serverless stream store that makes durable real-time streams feel as simple and scalable as object storage.
body_text: Elevate the beating heart of data systems. Our team has worked a lot on reliable real-time ingest, where The Log is foundational. We loved the serverless experience of object storage, but it simply did not exist for streaming data. We believe the humble log – the stream – deserves to be a cloud storage primitive. With S2, we are previewing just that: S2 is the Stream Store, our interpretation of streaming for the cloud era. What if streams had the primacy of objects? Object storage has been nothing short of revolutionary. S3 broke ground in 2006 with simple storage operations on named objects – and 18 years later, S3 Express One Zone even allows appends. But ultimately, object storage is all about blobs and byte ranges. It is best for data at rest. Our vision of stream storage is predicated on the idea that the demands of data in motion need a fresh perspective. With S2, you are elevated to the natural granularity of records . Writes to an S2 stream are appended at the tail, and even if multiple writers are acting at a time, S2 will durably sequence all records. S2 takes care of serving your reads efficiently, whether you need to start streaming from seconds ago or years. Streams can also be tailed in real-time, which is not possible with a blob in S3. Object Storage Stream Storage Blobs and byte ranges Records and sequence numbers PUT / GET / DELETE value of a named Object in a Bucket APPEND / READ / TRIM records on a named Stream in a Basin Cumbersome and expensive for granular appends Easy and cheap to append records Just like buckets are a namespace for objects, basins play that role for streams in S2. Basins and streams lean into the scale of the cloud – there is no limit on how many you can have, or how long data can be retained. Want to model streams per user? Do it, this isn't Kafka. There are no cluster limitations to wrangle, and no infrastructure to tune. $ s2 ls s2://copilot-rag-ingest user-foo/cool-project user-foo/another-project user-bar/fork-of-cool-project # ... ∞ This stream interface brought us closer to our vision, but we also wanted to liberate the superpower of offloading durability which databases like MemoryDB and Neon leverage. Decoupling compute and storage is safest when the storage service cooperates. So we added a verb to check the tail of the stream with strong consistency, and support for concurrency control when writing. You can be a pessimist wielding a fencing token or optimistically supply the sequence number you expect assigned – no judgment which side of the fence you find yourself on. Serverless – at what cost? S2 is architected around the infinite scale and unrelenting durability of object storage. That does not necessitate a slow or expensive offering – quite the opposite! We bridge the abstraction gap with a multi-tenant service so that you can have a truly serverless API for streaming data. Durability is not negotiable for us in the undeniable cloud storage triad . We allow users to navigate their latency vs cost tradeoff on a per stream basis, with storage classes . We are starting out with two: Standard , backed by S3 Standard in AWS. S3 Standard has a counterpart in all public cloud providers, so we will be able to ship it in all cloud regions as we grow. Express , backed by a quorum of three S3 Express One Zone buckets in AWS. Azure has had a regional counterpart for years, and it is in the cards at GCP, so we are optimistic about wider availability. Our Standard storage class provides end-to-end p99 latencies of under 500 milliseconds . With Express you can expect under 50 milliseconds – in the realm of disk-based cloud streaming systems! S2 on the other hand is completely diskless, and all writes will be safe in S3 with regional durability before being acknowledged. These latencies are supported at throughputs of hundreds of megabytes per second, per stream . The overhead of reading recently written data is negligible in S2 because of in-memory caching. Lagging readers can be particularly thirsty for throughput, and S2 serves them directly from object storage without a cap. We are initially throttling writes at 125 MiBps and reads against recent writes at 500 MiBps, per stream. The service is free during our preview period to optimize for feedback. We want to be transparent about our intended pricing , and you will find that S2 comes in meaningfully cheaper than the norms of cloud streaming systems. This will be particularly stark in comparison to "serverless" offerings, which attract tiny ceilings on the number of streams and the throughputs you can push through them – at a very high premium. There are no fixed costs in S2 like instances or cluster units. When we say serverless, we mean it! What's next for S2 S2 stands on a foundation of battle-tested cloud infrastructure, and our own Rust codebase gets put through the wringer with deterministic simulation testing. That said, the system is young, and there will be kinks. We are working hard to mature towards general availability and an SLA you can count on in production. We are now shipping a gRPC API, Rust SDK , and a shiny CLI – and we are going to get cracking on a REST API . Do tell us which language SDKs you would be most interested in. To give you a bigger picture sense of our direction: Kafka protocol compatibility . This will be an open source layer, and we will integrate certain features like key-based compaction directly in S2. Multi-region basins . Once we expand into more cloud regions, we see a path towards basins that can span regions and even clouds, for the highest standard of availability. Under 5 millisecond latencies . We are just getting started with the architectural flexibility of storage classes, and another 10x improvement over Express is achievable. Can you replace Kafka or Kinesis with S2 today? If you find yourself reaching for their “low-level” APIs, S2 is likely to be a fit, and even address your requirements more directly. If you expect a lot more from the cloud than current norms for streaming data – like not being limited on how many streams you can have, 10-100x higher ordered throughput, and concurrency control – S2 is the missing piece. We are beyond excited for all the innovative data systems S2 enables, and invite you to build with us !

title: 12 Powerful Use Cases of Generative AI in Customer Service

For more help, contact support.” Gen AI response in 2024 : “Hi Sally, your refund for Dyson Airwrap was processed on November 20th and should reach your account by November 28th. What is generative AI in customer service? Generative AI applies artificial intelligence to generate human-like responses and interact seamlessly with customers. It can create new content, including text, images, and music decoding patterns, making customer interactions more personalized and dynamic. This is done by learning from patterns in existing data and using that information to create contextually relevant answers on the spot. How does generative AI differ from conversational AI? To efficiently leverage the power of conversational and generative AI, you first have to understand their unique qualities. Conversational AI, as the name suggests, works best for on-the-spot talks, while generative AI’s specializes in generating original content from prompts given by humans. Basis Conversational AI Generative AI Core function Interactively communicates to handle predefined tasks like answering FAQs Creates new and unique content dynamically Technology Uses rule-based systems and Natural Language Understanding (NLU) Powered by advanced language models such as GPT to generate real-time responses Primary applications Customer support, educational bots, virtual assistants Content generation, media creation and design, data analysis Personalization Limited customization based on customer data Deep personalization by generating tailored responses Examples Chatbots, Siri, Alexa ChatGPT, Claude, Copy.ai Best for Straightforward, transactional tasks Creative or nuanced tasks 12 use cases of generative AI in customer service When we think of generative AI for customer service, we generally think of chatbots and instant answers. For example, if the customer sounds frustrated or annoyed in a conversation, the AI can immediately display empathy in its reply to calm the customer. This must have been frustrating for you. Let me look into the details and resolve this as quickly as possible. Thank you for your patience.” 4.Customized recommendations Gen AI for customer support can analyze user data such as purchase history, browsing behavior, and past interactions to understand customer needs and preferences. It then creates real-time tailored suggestions to make them feel more important. Music giant Spotify does it best by creating personalized playlists based on your musical preferences. Yourself” line to allow customers to make Funko figures of themselves and their loved ones. This is a unique way of using Gen AI to promote a connection with the brand by creating something personal. Source : Funko taking innovation to the next level with Gen AI 6.Multilanguage support Gen AI can handle multiple inquiries around the clock while identifying the language a customer is communicating with. It can translate conversations or even respond in multiple languages without needing pre-scripted answers for each language. The bot can then solve customer issues independently or transfer the conversation to a support agent who speaks the language. Airbnb uses Gen AI to translate texts from hosts and guests, ensuring clear communication across all languages. They also have a team of support executives who can speak multiple languages to escalate conversations whenever necessary. Source : Airbnb app does the best job in translation with Gen AI 7.Automated transcription Call transcripts are necessary for review, training, and quality assurance. Gen AI leverages advanced NLP and ML techniques to convert speech to text accurately. This is how it works: Process audio data to produce transcriptions even in noisy environments or varied accents Differentiate between multiple speakers in a conversation, assigning text to the correct person Use contextual understanding to transcribe industry-specific jargon, acronyms, and technical terms Generate summaries or highlight important information 8.Complaint resolution Gen AI can make complaint resolution more efficient through automation and generate more accurate responses and personalized solutions. It can quickly analyze and categorize customer complaints (e.g., delivery issues, product defects, service problems). Once a customer raises a complaint, Gen AI can instantly generate tailored responses and provide immediate acknowledgement about the issue being addressed. It can then suggest personalized resolution suggestions or escalate to a human agent by analyzing the severity of the issue. 9.Immersive training Businesses can incorporate Gen AI to refine training programs and offer instant and accurate customer service. It creates realistic scenarios and simulates customer interactions to provide employees with hands-on practice. Gen AI-driven training programs analyze historical customer data to identify regular customer problems and develop tailored training modules. This ensures customer reps gain the specific skills and knowledge required to deliver outstanding service. 10.Automated billing support Gen AI-powered automated billing systems can efficiently address the pressing pain areas in billing. It can even summarize reviews and categorize insights without manual effort. For example, if a user writes, “ The website is slow on mobile .” Gen AI immediately tags it as a “mobile usability issue.” 12.Appointment scheduling Traditional appointment scheduling is a time-consuming process that often requires customers to deal with long hold times and booking errors. title: Is vendor oversight *really* required, and why? - Blog - Affinity: Compliance and Learning Platform
body_text: As they say, it takes a village. And so with running a company, you can’t do it all on your own. ‍ So, you do the most logical thing: You spent your hard earned investor and revenue dollars to pay other companies to do the work for you. ‍ Or to put it nicely, you hire “vendors” to help run your business efficiently (your KYC tooling, your credit reporting agency, your servers). Not an earth shattering concept. We know all businesses have a supply chain somewhere behind that fancy logo. ‍ So what makes vendors so special in the world of fintech? ‍ Recall in our past post “ In a fintech-bank partnership, who is in charge? ”, regulators see the fintech as an extension of the bank (and not the other way around). ‍ To put it a bit more crudely for the fintech founders who might take exception to the description, the fintech is sort of like a vendor of the bank (providing marketing and customer acquisition services). ‍ And so when the fintech goes out and outsources some of its functions , the vendor is the vendor to the vendor of the bank. ‍ The chain is something like this: ‍ Regulators → oversee the bank sponsor Bank sponsor → oversees the fintech Fintech → oversees its vendors ‍ The way the regulators see it: Your vendor’s mistakes are your mistakes are the bank’s mistakes. And so, when working with a bank sponsor, you’ll get a lot of questions about your vendor oversight program. ‍ Are all vendors created equal though? Of course not. ‍ There are two types: (1) Critical vendors; and (2) Non-critical vendors ‍ Generally, a critical vendor is one that either: (1) has access to sensitive or confidential information of the company, including customer PII (personally identifiable information); or (2) is so critical to the functioning of the company that, if it were to go under, the company would have a major disruption in services. ‍ So your snack services company is likely not a critical vendor. But the credit reporting agency or outsourced ledgering service that has all your customer’s personal information on it servers probably is. ‍ If your vendor is “critical”, you need to assess how risky they are to your business and build in some protections in your contract. ‍ What does vendor oversight entail? It’s a combination of diligence, doing a legal review of your vendor agreement, and doing at least a once a year check in with the vendor (hey, vendor, you still kicking it? no data breaches last year, right?). ‍ How does this work in practice? ‍ Nowadays, you would probably send all your critical vendors a questionnaire that they would then fill out, and then resend it a year later, and so on. ‍ The questionnaire would ask questions like how long they’ve been in business, do they have basic controls like a SOC 2 certification, do they have an information security policy, do they have insurance, etc. ‍ If you are a solutions provider, you’re all too familiar with these questionnaires. And all these requirements have spawned an entire cottage industry of certification providers like SOC 2 providers (Vanta, Thoropass). ‍ Now, you might be wondering: Isn’t Amazon Web Services technically a “critical” vendor since, if their servers were to go down, your business would definitely be impacted. ‍ In theory, yes: ‍ But in practice? Good luck getting AWS to respond to your very important questionnaire. ‍ So, vendor oversight ends up being one of those murky areas of fintech that everyone says you should do but you really only do once you’re at a large enough scale. ‍ Until then, you just hope your vendors don’t have a data breach that is spilled over the news. ‍ As with all our posts, we like to include some practical tips for all you operators out there: ‍ If you’re an early stage fintech, you’re probably not going to do any vendor oversight, and that’s probably ok. Your bank sponsor will ask for it, and you’ll keep saying you’re going to do it but everyone knows you won’t ‍ If your fintech is at a critical size (usually, post PMF or Series A), you’re will have a formal vendor questionnaire that you’d send to all your critical (i.e., large) vendors ‍ If you scaling up up your fintech (Series C), you are likely hiring a dedicated role whose job is to deal with procurement and vendor oversight. ‍ If you’re the vendor that routinely gets flagged by your customers as “critical”, it is probably best to get in the habit of developing template answers for all those questionnaires you’ll be filling out, over and over and over again. ‍ ******************** While we hope you found this post helpful, please note that the information in this post is not intended to be legal or regulatory advice. title: Enlight & Clēnera Announce the Financial Close for Project Roadrunner
body_text: ‍ The debt financing package includes $550 million of construction loans Roadrunner consists of 290 MW of solar generation and 940 MWh of energy storage capacity, and is expected to reach full COD by the end of 2025 TEL AVIV, Israel, Dec. 23, 2024 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Enlight Renewable Energy Ltd. (“Enlight”, “the Company”, NASDAQ: ENLT, TASE: ENLT.TA), a leading global renewable energy platform, today announced that the Company has arranged the debt financing (the “Debt Financing”) for project Roadrunner (“Roadrunner” or “the Project”), located near Tucson, Arizona, USA As part of the Debt Financing, Enlight, through its subsidiary Clenera Holdings LLC, has entered into a loan agreement with a consortium of four leading global banks including BNP Paribas Securities Corp, Crédit Agricole, Natixis Commercial and Investment Bank, and Norddeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale (Nord/LB), totaling $550 million, which are expected to convert into a $290 million term loan and $320 million of tax equity funding upon the Project’s COD. The term loan is structured with an amortization tenor of 20-25 years and is to be fully repaid 5 years from the Project’s COD (mini perm). The loans are subject to an all-in interest rate of 5.50%-6.0%. The Company expects to conclude a tax equity transaction during 2025, noting that the project has secured safe harbor status. Paragon Energy Capital served as Clenera’s exclusive financial advisor on the transaction. Roadrunner (also known as Apache Solar II) is the second-largest project in Enlight’s history, consists of 290 MW solar generation and 940 MWh of energy storage capacity, and is expected to reach full COD by the end of 2025. Construction at the 1200-acre site has already begun, and all procurement contracts have been signed. The Project has a 20-year busbar power purchase agreement covering its entire output with the Arizona Electric Power Cooperative (AEPCO) and is expected to generate revenues of $51-54 million and EBITDA1 of $41-44 million in its first full year of operation. Roadrunner is being built in the Sulphur Springs Valley region near Tucson, Arizona. Arizona possesses one of highest rates of growth in data centers in the U.S., driving a significant increase in the demand for electricity. The area’s high altitude, mild weather, and very high irradiance make it especially suitable for a utility-scale solar plant. The Project is located in a sparsely populated area and integrates with the larger Apache Generating Station, a diverse energy complex used by AEPCO. After the completion of Apex in Montana and Atrisco in New Mexico, Roadrunner is one of several major solar and energy storage projects that Enlight and Clenera are now constructing in the U.S. These include Country Acres (392 MW and 688 MWh) and Quail Ranch (128 MW and 400 MWh). The two mega projects have almost completed their development phase, and are scheduled to begin construction in the coming months. Each of the two projects are set to achieve grid connection of 1.0 GW, one of the largest in the US. title: 6 benefícios de uma boa gestão de processos para sua empresa
summary: Descubra a importância e conheça os maiores benefícios de uma boa gestão de processos! Saiba como implementar a metodologia e transformar seu negócio
body_text: Os benefícios de uma boa gestão de processos vão muito além da organização e detalhamento das atividades executadas por uma companhia. Com a metodologia bem aplicada, é possível aumentar a produtividade, reduzir custos, implementar novas tecnologias, como a automação e inteligência artificial e, por fim, aumentar significativamente a receita. Aliás, a importância da gestão de processos está tão em voga que cada vez mais gestores buscam entender e investir em suas vantagens. Prova disso são os 11,83% de crescimento do setor previsto entre 2024 e 2029, quando estima-se que o mercado alcance o patamar dos US$ 26,17 bilhões. Ainda segundo a mesma pesquisa, publicada pelo Mordor Intelligence , o aumento nos valores investidos em gestão de processos acontece devido ao interesse das companhias em manter a competitividade na era da transformação digital. Para entender mais sobre os benefícios de uma boa gestão de processos e saber como implementá-la de forma eficiente, continue a leitura! A seguir, falamos sobre: o que é o gerenciamento de processos; qual a importância desse controle empresa; como implementar uma boa gestão de processos; como uma plataforma inteligente te ajuda nesse aspecto. O que é gestão de processos? Gestão de processos, termo traduzido de Business Process Management (BPM), é uma disciplina que envolve a análise, design, monitoramento e otimização de fluxos operacionais de uma organização. Seu principal objetivo é alinhar as atividades às metas da empresa e promover eficiência, agilidade e melhoria contínua em todas as etapas de desenvolvimento das tarefas. O uso de ferramentas de gerenciamento, os Business Process Management Suites (BPMS), é a melhor forma de conquistar os benefícios de uma boa gestão de processos. Esses softwares, quando bem configurados e alinhados aos objetivos do negócio, apresentam dados fundamentais para a aplicação de melhorias e novas tecnologias. Dessa forma, é possível implementar soluções, como a automação de tarefas, e aumentar tanto a produtividade quanto a satisfação geral dos consumidores com relação ao produto ou serviço ofertado. A importância da gestão de processos numa organização É essencial gerir os procedimentos e tarefas de forma eficiente para conquistar os benefícios de uma boa gestão de processos. Com essa metodologia, você mantém seu negócio competitivo e garante a qualidade dos seus produtos ou serviços, tem mais facilidade para fazer escolhas e mais liberdade para dispor recursos estrategicamente. Além disso, um dos principais pontos de importância da gestão de processos é a conformidade com as regulamentações. A implementação dessa disciplina garante que todas as etapas do fluxo operacional funcionem de acordo com as normas internas da companhia e das legislações vigentes. Assim, você reduz as chances de multas ou penalidades pelo não-cumprimento de alguma determinação ou regulamento, o que interfere tanto na qualidade da execução dos trabalhos quanto na forma como seus clientes e potenciais investidores enxergam a companhia. 6 benefícios de uma boa gestão de processos que você deve conhecer Aumento da produtividade As empresas eliminam processos redundantes e aumentam a eficiência operacional ao otimizar e automatizar as tarefas. Assim, o aproveitamento dos recursos torna-se estratégico, e os resultados, mais lucrativos. Redução de custos A redução de custos é uma consequência positiva de processos mais eficientes e permite a melhor alocação dos recursos disponíveis. Essa característica representa um dos principais benefícios de uma boa gestão de processos. Melhoria na qualidade e consistência É possível padronizar as tarefas e torná-las mais consistentes com o nível de qualidade exigido pelos consumidores por meio dos BPMS. Dessa forma, pode-se conquistar níveis mais altos de satisfação e, consequentemente, a fidelização do seu público. Mais agilidade e flexibilidade Outro importante benefício de uma boa gestão de processos é a possibilidade de agilizar as etapas de gerenciamento empresarial. Implementar a metodologia de gestão corretamente permite mudanças mais rápidas e flexíveis, para que a empresa se adapte tanto às novas metas quanto às mudanças de mercado. Mais segurança e conformidade Norma e leis — internas e externas— definem como deve ser a estrutura e a organização dos processos.Essa conformidade funciona como um fator de segurança, tanto para evitar problemas, quanto para seus consumidores e stakeholders. Melhoria contínua A melhoria contínua diz respeito ao conjunto de ações e estratégias que têm como objetivo o aperfeiçoamento da empresa. Ao aplicar uma boa gestão de processos, você tem um panorama completo do funcionamento das etapas para melhorá-las sempre que necessário. Como implementar uma boa gestão de processos em 5 etapas Tão importante quanto saber o que é gestão de processos, é saber como implementá-la. Para tal finalidade, existem, basicamente, 5 passos: identificação dos processos: identificar e entender a situação atual dos processos permite o seu mapeamento, bem como a exclusão de etapas desnecessárias e a realização de otimizações estratégicas; documentação: é imprescindível documentar as mudanças para transmiti-las aos demais setores do negócio. Dessa forma, os colaboradores entendem não apenas o que muda, mas também quais os seus papéis nas novas atribuições; análise e diagnóstico: uma vez documentado o novo fluxo, você deve analisá-lo para identificar ineficiências, gargalos e etapas desnecessárias, a fim realizar o processo com o máximo de eficiência e agilidade; implementação: defina um cronograma de implementação e inicie a aplicação das mudanças. Neste momento, é essencial realizar revisões periódicas para detectar falhas que passaram despercebidas, por exemplo; monitoramento e melhoria contínua: é possível identificar formas de otimizar os processos e atualizá-los para manter a conformidade e elevar a eficiência, sempre que necessário, por meio do monitoramento constante do fluxo de trabalho. Invista na transformação digital Uma das formas mais seguras de obter os benefícios de uma boa gestão de processos é investir em plataformas inteligentes , que organizam os fluxos de trabalho e oferecem dados sólidos para a evolução constante. Assim, mais do que garantir um aumento significativo na produtividade e mais satisfação nas entregas, você baseia suas futuras escolhas em informações atualizadas, com menos chances de erros. E ainda pode implementar outras soluções, como a automação ou inteligência artificial. Por isso, lembre-se: dê preferência a empresas idôneas e com resultados que são referência. Assim, mais do que melhorar a organização interna da companhia, você a torna mais competitiva e lucrativa. Este artigo foi escrito pela Lecom , empresa referência na Gestão Inteligente de Processos, oferecendo ao mercado uma plataforma de BPMS (Business Process Management Suite ou System) para automatizar, executar, melhorar e gerenciar processos.

Implementation of sophisticated improvements in the AI recommendation engine , resulting in enhanced content discoverability This latest investment aims to accelerate Anghami and OSN+'s growth trajectory, enabling the platforms to expand their content library, enhance user experience through cutting-edge technologies, and strengthen their presence across the MENA region. It is also aimed to drive innovations such as AI-driven personalization and next-generation streaming technologies. Elie Habib , CEO of Anghami and OSN+, said: "The success of this partnership is a testament to the power of collaboration and innovation. With this new investment from OSN Group, we are poised to elevate the digital entertainment experience for MENA audiences even further and expand our reach." Joe Kawkabani , CEO, OSN Group added: "This new round of funding reflects our unwavering belief in Anghami's potential to lead the MENA region in digital entertainment. Together, we will continue redefining how audiences experience premium content, ensuring our platform remains a pioneer in the industry." About Anghami Inc. (NASDAQ: ANGH ) : Anghami is the leading multi-media technology streaming platform in the Middle East and North Africa ("MENA") region, offering a comprehensive ecosystem of exclusive premium video, music, podcasts, live entertainment, audio services, and more. In a strategic move in April 2024 , Anghami joined forces with OSN+, a leading video streaming platform, forming a digital entertainment powerhouse. This pivotal transaction strengthened Anghami's position as a go-to destination, boasting an extensive library of over 18,000 hours of premium video, including exclusive HBO content, alongside 100+ million Arabic and International songs and podcasts. The OSN+ platform delivers the latest content at the same time as the US, including critically acclaimed must-see series and movies as well as world-class Arabic content and OSN+ Originals. With a user base exceeding 120 million registered users and 3.5 million paid subscribers, Anghami has partnered with 47 telcos across MENA, facilitating customer acquisition and subscription payment, in addition to establishing relationships with major film studios, entertainment giants, and music labels, both regional and international. Headquartered in Abu Dhabi , UAE, Anghami operates in 16 countries across MENA, with offices in Beirut , Dubai , Cairo , and Riyadh . To learn more about Anghami, please visit: https://anghami.com . About OSN Group OSN Group is the leading network for premium entertainment in the MENA region, operating in 22 countries featuring exclusive, in-demand global and local hit TV series and films as well as premium music offerings. OSN Group delivers content across multiple products: OSN+, OSNtv, Anghami and B2B offerings across the region. Home to the most compelling content from global studios, including Warner Bros. Discovery and NBCUniversal, OSN spearheads premium content including Western, Arabic, Turkish, and more across its divisions, distinctively known for exclusively broadcasting the latest HBO content on the same day as the US, including popular series, blockbuster movies, and the best in kids and lifestyle programming. OSN Group was formed in 2009 by the merger of the two largest subscription TV networks in the region, namely Orbit and Showtime Arabia, and is a subsidiary of KIPCO – Kuwait Projects Company (Holding).
